previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and dizziness, initially concerning for pulmonary embolism or heart failure. She had recently missed three days of Lovenox, and an ultrasound revealed a new deep vein thrombosis in the left deep peroneal vein. CT angiography ruled out pulmonary embolism, and echocardiogram showed hyperdynamic left ventricular function with mild outflow obstruction and moderate hypertrophy, but no acute cardiac cause for symptoms. Her shortness of breath was attributed to a resolving upper respiratory infection. Orthostatic hypotension and mild acute kidney injury were secondary to decreased oral intake and resolved with IV fluids. Lovenox was continued at a reduced dose of 80 mg daily due to a supratherapeutic level. The patient improved clinically and was discharged home with follow-up planned with her oncology team.
problems: Acute venous embolism and thrombosis of deep vessels of distal lower extremity
Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site

with new bruising. You had been taking a blood thinning 
medication (lovenox) and we felt it was responsible for the

ulcer in your stomach and inflammation of your stomach lining, 
and internal hemorrhoids. Please continue taking your antacids 
at home, as this should help treat your ulcer. Please do not 
drink alcohol or take aspirin, ibuprofen, or other NSAIDs as 
these can make your stomach ulcer worse.
